newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso ends firm, rate hike expected.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso ends firm, rate hike expected.

text.p: Mexican same-day peso contracts closed firmer on Tuesday after local brokers sold dollars ahead of an expected hike in domestic primary rates, traders said.
"The peso was boosted by hikes expected in Cetes rates at the primary auction which will make real returns attractive enough to draw in capital," a peso trader said.

The same-day peso closed 5.2 centavos firmer at 7.5280/7.5320 per dollar. Traders put the difference down to the fact that same-day contracts had lagged behind late changes in other contracts on Monday.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were both meanwhile 0.9 centavos firmer at 7.5340/7.5375 and 7.5315/7.5340 per dollar, respectively.
Traders said they expected trade to be slow until the Federal Open Market Committee meeting announces a decision on U.S. interest rates, expected at 1315 local time/1415 EDT.
